1.explanation:
All of the logic around sizing and sorting lives in the React DataTable wrapper: 

• DataTable.js is the top-level component that accepts the size prop and figures out which headers are sortable; it should flag the underlying <Table> with a new sortable prop when any header is sorted, but currently it doesn’t.  
• Table.js is responsible for rendering the <table> element with the right CSS classnames (e.g. bx--data-table--tall, and in v7+ a bx--table--sortable class). Without passing sortable into this component, the tall-variant sort styles never get applied.  
• TableHeader.js actually renders the <th> and the sort icon; it needs to adjust its internal spacing or vertical-alignment when inside a tall table or when the sortable class is present. Because neither Table nor TableHeader toggles the new “sortable” styling or alignment rules for tall tables, the label/icon combination floats out of sync with the other headers.
1.bug_scenario: When you set the DataTable size to “tall” and enable sorting on one or more columns (via getHeaderProps({ header, isSortable: true })), the header label and its sort icon become vertically misaligned compared to the other, non-sortable headers. In the screenshot you can see that the “Name” header (which is sortable) sits a few pixels higher than the “Description”, “Status”, and “Start Date” headers when using the tall row height.

2.explanation:
• DataTable.js: this is the top‐level React component. It accepts the size prop (e.g. "tall") and is responsible for forwarding it into the table rendering pipeline. If it doesn’t propagate size correctly, the rest of the table (notably the sortable headers) won’t receive the necessary class names to trigger the tall-variant CSS.  
• Table.js: renders the <table> element and applies modifier classes such as bx--table--tall based on the size prop. If the tall class is missing or mis‐named here, the CSS that centers the sort‐button content in tall rows never applies.  
• TableHeader.js: renders each <th> and, when isSortable is true, wraps its contents in the bx--table-sort <button>. Currently it doesn’t detect the tall context and so the inner button keeps the default vertical padding (for normal rows) and ends up misaligned in padding‐increased tall rows.  
• data-table.scss: contains the CSS rules for both the tall table variant and the sort‐button styling. It needs a new rule (or adjustment) under the .bx--table--tall modifier so that .bx--table-sort elements (and their child icon + label spans) are vertically centered in the taller header row.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a carbon DataTable with size="tall" and enable sorting on one or more columns, the header cells that are wrapped in the sort‐button become vertically misaligned compared to the plain header cells. In the screenshot the “Name” header (sortable) sits slightly lower than “Description”, “Status”, and “Start Date” (non‐sortable), even though the row height has increased for the tall variant.
